display.title: Tanya Shiur 29b: Modeh Ani, the Beinoni in Tanya Chapter 13 and the Shofar (Elul)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur: Modeh Ani in the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch, Tanya chapter 13 on how the beinoni differs from the tzaddik and the rasha, and why a simple ram's horn crowns Hashem on Rosh Hashanah.
display.summary_long: The next week's shiur in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, given the day after Chai Elul. It opens at the end of Rabbi Akiva's story 'all that Hashem does is for the good' and explains 'Shivisi' as treating every event and every mitzvah alike, with fresh enthusiasm each morning, as if the Torah were given today. Shulchan Aruch HaRav 1:5-6 follows: saying Modeh Ani on waking, thanking Hashem for returning a renewed soul, pausing a moment before standing up, and why Modeh Ani may be said before washing the hands. Tanya chapter 13 then shows how the beinoni acts exactly like a tzaddik yet still has desire for worldly pleasures, and why he should regard himself 'like a rasha' even when the whole world calls him a tzaddik. A Rosh Hashanah talk explains that only a Jew can make Hashem King, and why the shofar is a plain, unadorned ram's horn with a simple sound: the animal soul itself proclaims Hashem King. It closes with the Rebbe's Chai Elul talk on the Baal Shem Tov's question about blessings that lead to teshuvah.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with fresh enthusiasm every day, and bring even the animal soul to accept Him as King.
